:::{#thm-source-coding}
#### Source coding theorem

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv)
that takes a finite number of values, at least two of them with nonzero [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability),
and let $H_2(X)$ be its
[entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy)
with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm).

1. Every [uniquely decodable](#def-uniquely-decodable) [binary code](#def-code) for $X$
   has [expected length](#def-expected-length) $L \ge H_2(X)$.

2. Some uniquely decodable binary code for $X$ has expected length
   $L < H_2(X) + 1$.

3. Coding $n$ [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) copies of $X$ at a time,
   some uniquely decodable binary code spends, on average,
   fewer than $H_2(X) + 1/n$ binary digits per copy.

:::
